subject: The same model works with RW1 and RW2 but not with AR1

messages.author: cd79aec8f4be0778
messages.subject: The same model works with RW1 and RW2 but not with AR1
parts:
Hello everyone,

I'm trying to analyze some temporal data with a model that has a large number of parameters. To account for the temporal component, I have executed exactly the same model with a Random Walk of order 2 (RW2), another with RW1, and finally another with Autoregressive of order 1 (AR1).

For both RW2 and RW1, I can consider the following strategies and they work correctly. ctrl.inla = list(int.strategy = "grid", strategy = "laplace"). The problem arises with AR1, where the only integration strategy that works is "EB," and I can't execute it with the "grid" strategy. As I mentioned, it is EXACTLY the same model as RW2 or RW1; I simply changed the "model" option within the "f" components.

The model:

naturals ~ -1 + f(dow, model = "iid", hyper = list(prec = list(initial = log(1e-04),
    fixed = TRUE))) + cb1 + cb2 + cb3 + cb4 + cb5 + cb6 + cb7 +
    cb8 + cb9 + cb10 + cb11 + cb12 + cb13 + cb14 + cb15 + cb16 +

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] The same model works with RW1 and RW2 but not with AR1
parts:
If you upgrade to most recent testing version, you should be fine. The number of hyperparameters allowed has been increased

Maybe you want to add int.strategy=‘eb’ if this take to long time 

—
Haavard Rue
Helpdesk
he...@r-inla.org
On 20 Mar 2024 at 15:59 +0300, Marc <mmari...@gmail.com>, wrote:

Hello everyone,

I'm trying to analyze some temporal data with a model that has a large number of parameters. To account for the temporal component, I have executed exactly the same model with a Random Walk of order 2 (RW2), another with RW1, and finally another with Autoregressive of order 1 (AR1).

For both RW2 and RW1, I can consider the following strategies and they work correctly. ctrl.inla = list(int.strategy = "grid", strategy = "laplace"). The problem arises with AR1, where the only integration strategy that works is "EB," and I can't execute it with the "grid" strategy. As I mentioned, it is EXACTLY the same model as RW2 or RW1; I simply changed the "model" option within the "f" components.

On 20 Mar 2024 at 15:59 +0300, Marc <mmari...@gmail.com>, wrote:

Hello everyone,

I'm trying to analyze some temporal data with a model that has a large number of parameters. To account for the temporal component, I have executed exactly the same model with a Random Walk of order 2 (RW2), another with RW1, and finally another with Autoregressive of order 1 (AR1).

For both RW2 and RW1, I can consider the following strategies and they work correctly. ctrl.inla = list(int.strategy = "grid", strategy = "laplace"). The problem arises with AR1, where the only integration strategy that works is "EB," and I can't execute it with the "grid" strategy. As I mentioned, it is EXACTLY the same model as RW2 or RW1; I simply changed the "model" option within the "f" components.

On 20 Mar 2024 at 15:59 +0300, Marc <mmari...@gmail.com>, wrote:

Hello everyone,

I'm trying to analyze some temporal data with a model that has a large number of parameters. To account for the temporal component, I have executed exactly the same model with a Random Walk of order 2 (RW2), another with RW1, and finally another with Autoregressive of order 1 (AR1).

For both RW2 and RW1, I can consider the following strategies and they work correctly. ctrl.inla = list(int.strategy = "grid", strategy = "laplace"). The problem arises with AR1, where the only integration strategy that works is "EB," and I can't execute it with the "grid" strategy. As I mentioned, it is EXACTLY the same model as RW2 or RW1; I simply changed the "model" option within the "f" components.

The model:

Eating naturals ~ -1 + f(dow, model = "iid", hyper = list(prec = list(initial = log(1e-04),
fixed = TRUE))) + cb1 + cb2 + cb3 + cb4 + cb5 + cb6 + cb7 +
cb8 + cb9 + cb10 + cb11 + cb12 + cb13 + cb14 + cb15 + cb16 +
cb17 + cb18 + cb19 + cb20 + f(id_cb_rw1, cb1, model = "ar1") +
f(id_cb_rw2, cb2, model = "ar1") + f(id_cb_rw3, cb3, model = "ar1") +

parts:
its not an 'error', its that the internal integration tables are not
buildt for that many hyperparameters.

try with int.strategy='eb' ?

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] The same model works with RW1 and RW2 but not with AR1
parts: Understood, I will use the same type of integration method (EB) and approximation (Laplace) for all the models that I compare. Thank you very much for your help!

I would be careful to compare two models with: one with integration and
one without. I think they should be 'treated' similarly.
